subject: general
question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 17 years. In how many years will it amount to 81 times of itself?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **t** years, it becomes **nk** times in **k × t** years.

Here, the sum becomes **3 times** in **17 years** (n = 3, t = 17).

We need the sum to become **81 times**, which is **3⁴** (so, k = 4).

Required time = **k × t** = 4 × 17 = **68 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 68 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b45840426f859ecce5004d9c29d91d6e776bca2eb3f1908f4174255734bebe2e.png] 

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** triples in 17 years ⇒ **Amount (A₁)** = 3P

**Time (T₁)** = 17 years

**Target Amount (A₂)** = 81P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁷

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)¹⁷ --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Let the required time be **T** years for the sum to become 81 times.

⇒ 81P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 81 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 3⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ Substituting the value of 3 from Eq. 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁷]⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)¹⁷ × ⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ T = 68 years

**∴ The correct answer is 68 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Growth

In **Compound Interest**, the amount increases **geometrically**. If it becomes 'x' times in 't' years, it will become 'x²' in 2t years and 'x³' in 3t years.

Simple Interest Growth

In **Simple Interest**, the growth is **arithmetic**. If a sum triples (becomes 3P) in 17 years, it means interest for 17 years is 2P. To become 81 times (80P interest), it would take (80/2) × 17 = 680 years.

Effective Rate for Compounding

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate is halved (r/2) and the time period is doubled (2t) in the standard CI formula.</p
